_meta: Lead-chasing follow-up round after AF/G.23, 2026-08-13. Transcribes verified findings supplied for this round (no new web research performed by this session). Resolves two of the three foundational-law leads gq-g23-municipal.json's _dropped block left open from LPGE 2023's Exposición de Motivos ('la Ley de Finanzas Públicas, la Ley Tributaria'): the tax code is now identified, dated and minted from a verbatim citation in the FY2026 budget law's own Article 14; the public-finance law's title/number/date is now confirmed but its full text remains unlocated, so it stays a _dropped lead rather than a node. Also closes gq-g23-municipal.json's outstanding 'Ley 1/2003 vs Ley 1/2013' discrepancy (see the UPDATE note prepended to gq-ley-1-2003-administracion-local's description in that file) and records the specific access failures hit this round so future sessions do not repeat them.

reports.title: Ley Núm. 1/2024, de fecha 19 de noviembre, General Tributaria en la República de Guinea Ecuatorial
reports.description: The current, in-force general tax code, superseding the prior Ley Número 4/2.004 (see gq-ley-4-2004-sistema-tributario). Its own primary text was not independently located or downloaded this round — this node is minted from a verbatim citation in the FY2026 national budget law (Ley Número 9/2025, LPGE 2026), independently downloaded via direct PDF download and full-text-searched via pdftotext/grep this round: Artículo 14 states "Las obligaciones tributarias para el Régimen Especial de Actividades Menores, establecidas en los artículos 94 de la Ley Núm. 1/2024, de fecha 19 de noviembre, General Tributaria en la República de Guinea Ecuatorial y de la Ley de Tasas Fiscales y Precios Públicos en la República de Guinea Ecuatorial, quedan fijadas conforme a la actualización..." This confirms the law's exact number, date and short title, and that it is currently cited as in-force law by the FY2026 budget (a document dated after this law's own 19 November 2024 enactment). CAVEAT ON SOURCING, per this branch's established convention for citation-only mints (same tier as cemac-underlying-inflation-regulation in af-grok-synthesis.json): this is a title/date/description reached via a citing document, not a self-standing primary read of the tax code's own text — flagged honestly rather than presented as more thoroughly sourced than it is. A second law is also named in the same Article 14 clause, "la Ley de Tasas Fiscales y Precios Públicos en la República de Guinea Ecuatorial" (a fees/public-prices law), not yet a node — see _dropped.
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational tax-code law (a recast/successor instrument, superseding Ley 4/2004 of 2004).

reports.title: Ley Número 4/2.004, de fecha 28 de Octubre, Reguladora del Sistema Tributario
reports.description: The prior general tax code, in force from 2004 until superseded by Ley Núm. 1/2024 (gq-ley-1-2024-general-tributaria; see that node's description and the _dropped entry below on the unconfirmed supersession text). Its own preamble, independently downloaded and pdftotext-verified this round, states: "...mediante el Decreto-Ley número 1/1986, de fecha 10 de febrero, se adoptó el Sistema Tributario de Guinea Ecuatorial..." — naming its own predecessor, a 1986 decree-law, the same pattern gq-ley-1-2003-administracion-local's own preamble shows for the local-administration branch. CAVEAT ON SOURCING: the government's own former host for this text (minhacienda-gob.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/LEY-TRIBUTARIA-1.pdf) now returns 404 after a site rebuild (see _dropped); the only text located this round is a third-party WordPress mirror (leydeguinea.wordpress.com), not a government domain. Treated as usable primary-source text under this branch's established convention for verbatim-government-text-via-third-party-hosting (the same tier applied to gw-lei-7-96-financas-locais's vlex.pt sourcing and to droit-afrique.com/WIPO Lex mirrors elsewhere in this project) because the text reproduced is the government-authored statute itself, not a paraphrase — flagged explicitly rather than silently. No `source_kind` set (defaults to `official`), consistent with that convention: the hosting is third-party, but the content is not commercial.
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational tax-code law, superseded 2024 (see gq-ley-1-2024-general-tributaria).

reports.title: Ley Número 9/2025, de los Presupuestos Generales del Estado para el Ejercicio Económico 2026 (LPGE 2026)
reports.publisher: Ministerio de Hacienda y Presupuestos — República de Guinea Ecuatorial
reports.description: Equatorial Guinea's FY2026 national budget law, following gq-ley-8-2022-pge-2023 (FY2023). Fills the lead that node's own cadence_note flagged ('A later LPGE 2026 draft (ahoraeg.com) was located in secondary search but not independently downloaded/full-text-searched this round') — this round independently downloaded the government's own minhacienda-gob.com-hosted PDF and full-text-searched it via pdftotext/grep, superseding the earlier ahoraeg.com secondary-source draft reference. Its own preamble states: "Los Presupuestos Generales del Estado para el año 2026 se han elaborado dentro del marco de la Ley Fundamental de Guinea Ecuatorial, así como de la Ley de Finanzas Públicas, donde se establece que la elaboración, aprobación y ejecución de los presupuestos... se realizarán en un marco de estabilidad presupuestaria" — naming the Constitution and the Ley de Finanzas Públicas as foundational inputs, echoing LPGE 2023's own Exposición de Motivos pattern (gq-ley-8-2022-pge-2023 -> gq-ley-fundamental). Artículo 14 separately fixes tax obligations for the Régimen Especial de Actividades Menores 'conforme a la actualización' of Ley Núm. 1/2024 (General Tributaria) and the Ley de Tasas Fiscales y Precios Públicos — see gq-ley-1-2024-general-tributaria. Exact enactment date ('de fecha...') not confirmed this round; the law number (9/2025) places enactment in 2025.
reports.cadence_note: Annual national budget law; this is the Ejercicio Económico 2026 edition.

dependencies.basis: LPGE 2026's own Artículo 14 fixes tax obligations for the Régimen Especial de Actividades Menores 'conforme a la actualización' of provisions 'establecidas en los artículos 94 de la Ley Núm. 1/2024, de fecha 19 de noviembre, General Tributaria en la República de Guinea Ecuatorial' — naming the tax code directly by number and date as the basis for the obligations it fixes, without itself replacing the tax code's own mechanism (hence cites rather than a computational relationship type).

LPGE 2026's own preamble states the budget 'se han elaborado dentro del marco de la Ley Fundamental de Guinea Ecuatorial, así como de la Ley de Finanzas Públicas' — naming the Constitution directly as a foundational input, the same pattern already documented for gq-ley-8-2022-pge-2023 -> gq-ley-fundamental.

_dropped.why: Title, number and date are now confirmed: "LEY 9/2003 — REGULADORA DE LAS FINANZAS PÚBLICAS DEL ESTADO DE GUINEA ECUATORIAL" (13 November 2003), per Ministerio de Hacienda y Presupuestos's own current site (https://minhacienda-gob.com/derecho-financiero/), and corroborated independently by LPGE 2026's own preamble naming 'la Ley de Finanzas Públicas' as a framework input alongside the Ley Fundamental. This upgrades the corresponding LPGE-2023-round lead (gq-g23-municipal.json _dropped: 'gq-ley-8-2022-pge-2023 -> Ley de Finanzas Públicas', reason no-document) from an unnamed generic reference to an exact citation — but the law's full article text still was not located this round. boe.gob.gq (Equatorial Guinea's official Boletín Oficial del Estado portal, the natural authoritative host) could not be reached this round: TLS certificate validation failed on every attempt. All direct download-URL guesses on minhacienda-gob.com's own upload directories (mirroring the pattern of the successful LPGE-2026 and derecho-financiero URLs) returned 404 — the site appears to have been rebuilt since the law was last hosted there, and no working direct link to the full text was found by URL-guessing. A strong, precisely-numbered lead for a future round: search minhacienda-gob.com's current site structure directly (not URL-guessing) for 'Ley 9/2003' or 'Ley de Finanzas Públicas', or retry boe.gob.gq once its certificate issue is resolved.

Ley 1/2024 is titled 'General Tributaria' and dated 19 November 2024, two decades after Ley 4/2004's 'Reguladora del Sistema Tributario'; a general recast of the entire tax code arriving two decades after the prior one, cited as the current basis for tax obligations in a 2026 budget law, is very plausibly a formal repeal-and-replace of Ley 4/2004. But this is inference from timing and titling, not a textual finding: neither law's own text (Ley 1/2024's, not independently located this round beyond its Article-14 citation; Ley 4/2004's own third-party-mirrored text, independently checked this round) states a repeal of the other in the passages read. A `RelationType: supersedes` entry was deliberately not created because it requires quoting the instrument verbatim, per Relation's own schema comment, and no such verbatim repeal clause was located. A lead for a future round: locate Ley 1/2024's own preamble/derogatory clause (typically the article that explicitly repeals the prior law) to confirm.

UPDATE 2026-08-13 (AF lead-chase round): two candidate targets are now identified and minted — gq-ley-1-2024-general-tributaria and gq-ley-4-2004-sistema-tributario — but LPGE 2023 (Ley Número 8/2022, de fecha 13 de octubre 2022) predates Ley 1/2024's 19 November 2024 enactment by over two years, so 'la Ley Tributaria' as named in LPGE 2023's own Exposición de Motivos almost certainly refers to the then-operative Ley 4/2004, not Ley 1/2024. This is a dating argument, not a textual naming: LPGE 2023's own passage names 'la Ley Tributaria' generically, without a law number, so no edge is drawn without over-interpreting what the source document actually states — per the evidence-strict citation rule, a plausible identification is recorded here as a lead rather than asserted as a documented edge. A future round drawing this edge should cite the reasoning above explicitly in `basis` if it proceeds.
